# Introduction

Single-cell multiomics technologies allow simultaneous or parallel measurement of multiple
cellular features — most commonly gene expression (scRNA-seq) and chromatin accessibility
(scATAC-seq). Simulating multiomics data presents unique challenges because algorithms must
preserve not only the distinct statistical properties of each individual modality, but also
the biological coupling and regulatory relationships between them.

`scSimEval` is designed to evaluate simulation fidelity across **two primary multiomics
experimental designs**, each tailored to the level of cell-level pairing between modalities:
**Paired Multiomics** (co-assay profiling of identical individual cells) and **Unpaired Multiomics**
(independent profiling of separate cells from the same biological system). Understanding which design
your simulated data belongs to is essential for selecting the correct evaluation functions.

---

# Part 1: Understanding Multiomics Data Types

## 1.1 Paired Multiomics (Co-assay)

**Definition:** Both scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq are measured **simultaneously from the exact
same individual cells**. Each cell barcode in the RNA matrix has a corresponding and biologically
meaningful entry at the same column index in the ATAC matrix.

**Technologies:** 10x Chromium Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq, Paired-seq, ASTAR-seq

**Simulators:** scMultiSim (Li et al., *Nat Methods* 2023), SymSim2+ATAC, MultiSim

**What scSimEval can evaluate:**

* ✅ Full unimodal evaluation for each modality (Categories 1–5, 7, and 8)
* ✅ **All** Category 6 multiomics integration & alignment metrics (`evaluate_multiomics_integration()`):
  * `batch_asw` (Batch Average Silhouette Width in joint embedding space)
  * `cell_type_asw` (Cell-Type Average Silhouette Width in joint embedding space)
  * `graph_connectivity` (Within-cell-type k-NN graph connectivity)
  * `ari` (Adjusted Rand Index on joint latent clustering)
  * `nmi` (Normalized Mutual Information on joint latent clustering)

---

## 1.2 Unpaired Multiomics (Independent profiling)

**Definition:** scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq are profiled **from different cells** derived from
the same biological tissue, cell line, or sample. Cell barcodes do **not** correspond between
modalities — column *i* of the RNA matrix and column *i* of the ATAC matrix represent
entirely different cells.

**Technologies:** Bulk ATAC + scRNA-seq, independent 10x scATAC + scRNA experiments on
the same tissue, sci-ATAC-seq paired with scRNA-seq on sibling aliquots

**Simulators:** scDesign3, scMultiSim, scCross

**What scSimEval can evaluate:**

* ✅ Full unimodal evaluation for each modality independently (Categories 1–5, 7, and 8)
* ✅ Joint-embedding multiomics integration metrics (Category 6) when pre-integrated embeddings (`integrated` or `pca`) are supplied on the combined multiomics object via `pairing = "unpaired"` in `evaluate_multiomics_accuracy()`.

---

## 1.3 Metric Compatibility Summary

| Metric / Function | Paired | Unpaired |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| `evaluate_simulation_accuracy()` per modality | ✅ | ✅ |
| `evaluate_clustering_metrics()` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `evaluate_batch_metrics()` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `evaluate_deg_fidelity()` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `evaluate_trajectory_metrics()` *(scRNA-seq only)* | ✅ | ✅ |
| `evaluate_multiomics_integration()` | ✅ | ✅ (via joint embedding) |
| **`evaluate_multiomics_accuracy()`** | ✅ (`pairing = "paired"`) | ✅ (`pairing = "unpaired"`) |

---

# Part 2: Evaluating Paired Multiomics

## 2.1 Loading the Example Paired Dataset

`scSimEval` includes a paired scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq dataset (`example_multiomics`) where
every column in the RNA matrix corresponds to the same cell in the ATAC matrix:

```{r setup}
library(scSimEval)

# Load packaged paired multiomics example dataset
data(example_multiomics)

cat("Reference RNA dimensions:", dim(example_multiomics$ref_multi$rna), "\n")
cat("Reference ATAC dimensions:", dim(example_multiomics$ref_multi$atac), "\n")
cat("Simulated RNA dimensions:", dim(example_multiomics$sim_multi$rna), "\n")
cat("Simulated ATAC dimensions:", dim(example_multiomics$sim_multi$atac), "\n")
cat("Cell types:", levels(example_multiomics$cell_types), "\n")
```

The dataset contains:

* `ref_multi`: Named list `rna` (count matrix) and `atac` (peak accessibility matrix),
  both measured from the **same cells**.
* `sim_multi`: Simulated paired `rna` and `atac` matrices.
* `cell_types`: Cell type annotations shared across both modalities.
* `batch_info`: Batch labels shared across both modalities.
* `resource_stats`: Hardware logs (runtime in seconds and peak RAM in MiB).

---

## 2.2 Multiomics Integration & Alignment (Category VI)

Category VI evaluates multiomics integration and biological preservation using gold-standard metrics from `scib`, `scMultiSim`, `scCross`, `Matilda`, and `scMoMtF`:

```{r integration-eval}
int_res <- evaluate_multiomics_integration(
  ref_multi  = example_multiomics$ref_multi,
  sim_multi  = example_multiomics$sim_multi,
  cell_types = example_multiomics$cell_types,
  batch_info = example_multiomics$batch_info,
  verbose    = FALSE
)

print(int_res$integration_summary_table)
```

---

## 2.3 Master Paired Pipeline: `evaluate_multiomics_accuracy()`

For fully paired data, the master function coordinates all 8 categories:

```{r master-multi}
master_eval <- evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(
  ref_multi  = example_multiomics$ref_multi,
  sim_multi  = example_multiomics$sim_multi,
  cell_types = example_multiomics$cell_types,
  elapsed_time = example_multiomics$resource_stats$elapsed_time,
  memory_mb    = example_multiomics$resource_stats$memory_mb,
  verbose      = FALSE
)

head(master_eval$benchmark_summary_table)
```

> **Parallel Multi-Core Acceleration (`threads`):**
> On multi-core systems or HPC nodes, set `threads = 4` or `threads = 8` to accelerate
> the dual unimodal layer evaluations and Category 6 cross-modal correlation computations
> across CPU worker threads via `BiocParallel`.

---

# Part 3: Evaluating Unpaired Multiomics

For unpaired data, scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq come from **different cells**. The recommended
workflow is to evaluate each modality independently and combine results.

## 3.1 Step-by-Step Workflow for Unpaired Data

```r
library(scSimEval)
data(example_scrna)   # RNA modality
data(example_scatac)  # ATAC modality (different cells)

# ── Step 1: Evaluate each modality independently ──────────────────────────────
rna_eval <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(
  ref_data = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data = example_scrna$sim,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

atac_eval <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(
  ref_data = example_scatac$ref,
  sim_data = example_scatac$sim,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# ── Step 2: Consolidate and compare across modalities ─────────────────────────
dataset_collection <- list(
  "Method_A-RNA"  = list(ref = example_scrna$ref,  sim = example_scrna$sim),
  "Method_A-ATAC" = list(ref = example_scatac$ref, sim = example_scatac$sim)
)

consolidated <- evaluate_multiple_datasets(
  datasets          = dataset_collection,
  pair_by_prefix    = TRUE,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose           = FALSE
)

print(consolidated$dataset_overview)
```

---

# Part 4: Visualization

`scSimEval` visualization functions work seamlessly across unimodal, paired, and unpaired multiomics configurations:

```r
# Multi-dataset consolidated benchmark bubble matrix
plot_benchmark_bubble_matrix(
  data  = consolidated,
  title = "Benchmarking Multiomics Simulators"
)

# Evaluation summary horizontal bar matrix
plot_evaluation_summary(
  data  = consolidated,
  title = "Multiomics Simulator Leaderboard"
)
```

## 4.1 Low-Dimensional Multiomics Cell Embeddings

To visually examine whether simulated cells maintain the biological manifold of empirical data across modalities, researchers can project reference and simulated cells into low-dimensional UMAP, t-SNE, or PCA coordinates:

```{r multiomics-embeddings-demo, eval=TRUE}
# Compute low-dimensional embeddings for the scRNA-seq modality
emb_rna <- compute_dataset_embeddings(
  reference   = example_multiomics$ref_multi$rna,
  simulated   = list("Multi_Sim" = example_multiomics$sim_multi$rna),
  reduction   = "pca",
  n_pcs       = 5,
  cell_types  = example_multiomics$cell_types
)

# Plot multiomics cell embeddings
plot_dataset_embeddings(
  embedding_data = emb_rna,
  reduction      = "pca",
  layout         = "side_by_side",
  color_by       = "cell_type"
)

# Quantitative embedding quality metrics
knitr::kable(compute_embedding_quality_metrics(emb_rna), digits = 4)
```

---

# Part 5: Summary

| Data Type | Example Technologies | `evaluate_multiomics_accuracy()` | Category 6 Metrics | Recommended Function |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| **Paired** | 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq | ✅ `pairing = "paired"` | All 5 Category VI integration metrics (`batch_asw`, `cell_type_asw`, `graph_connectivity`, `ari`, `nmi`) | `evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(..., pairing = "paired")` |
| **Unpaired** | Independent scRNA + scATAC | ✅ `pairing = "unpaired"` | Joint-embedding integration metrics + per-modality unimodal evaluation | `evaluate_multiomics_accuracy(..., pairing = "unpaired")` |
